findings.issue_text: useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities which hardcodes isFederated = false, so callers lose federated-rule protection and Update/Delete/Pause become supported for rules in federated Mimir groups

In useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, when rule is undefined (skipToken path) loading is false so MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported, causing Duplicate to resolve as supported for non-existent rules; AlertRuleMenu ORs this with the ruler result so Mimir/Loki rules show Duplicate whenever the user has Grafana create permission, even when ruler ability said NotSupported. Skip path should return all-NotSupported

GrafanaGroupLoader removed the ruler query, dropping the 'Creating' (ruler-only) and 'Deleting' (prom-only) states; rules in the ruler not yet propagated to Prometheus silently don't appear, and tests covering these states were deleted rather than adapted
GrafanaRuleListItem href no longer includes returnTo (old GrafanaRuleLoader used createRelativeUrl with returnTo), losing back-navigation context when navigating from list to rule view

GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx 'correct menu actions' test grants AlertingRuleDelete permission and defines a delete selector but asserts exactly 4 items and never checks for Delete; either Delete is broken via the prom-rule ability path or the '4 menu actions' comment is wrong; needs explicit assertion on Delete presence/absence

AlertRuleMenu runs both useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities unconditionally for every rule, doubling ability computation and adding a useFolder subscription per rule in a hot component; prefer prom path only when rulerRule is absent
useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities/useRulerRuleAbilities memoize on actions, but AlertRuleMenu call sites pass inline array literals so the useMemo cache misses every render

RuleActionsButtons.V2 getEditableIdentifier calls logWarning inside render and returns undefined, firing a warning on every re-render for datasource prom rules without a ruler rule and silently hiding all action buttons with no user feedback

useAllAlertRuleAbilities @deprecated note steers callers to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which is functionally weaker due to missing federated handling; deprecation note should not recommend it until federated handling is restored

goldens.comment: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.

RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities which hardcodes isFederated = false, so callers lose federated-rule protection and Update/Delete/Pause become supported for rules in federated Mimir groups

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` to simply compute a `groupIdentifierV2` and delegate to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`. In `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, the previous federated protection logic is removed and replaced with a hardcoded `const isFederated = false; // TODO: Add support for federated rules`. Since `immutableRule` is computed as `isProvisioned || isFederated || isPluginProvided`, federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable, which can make Update/Delete/Pause/etc. appear supported/allowed when `isEditable/isRemovable` are true. This is a concrete behavior change visible in the diff and matches the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, when rule is undefined (skipToken path) loading is false so MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported, causing Duplicate to resolve as supported for non-existent rules; AlertRuleMenu ORs this with the ruler result so Mimir/Loki rules show Duplicate whenever the user has Grafana create permission, even when ruler ability said NotSupported. Skip path should return all-NotSupported

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken, actions)` in `AlertRuleMenu` and then ORs each ability with the corresponding ruler ability. In `useAbilities.ts`, `skipToken` maps to `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)`. When `rule` is `undefined`, `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` returns `{isEditable:false,isRemovable:false,loading:false}`, so `MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported` (because `loading` is false). That makes abilities like `Duplicate` supported even with no rule instance, and `allowed` is computed from global `getRulesPermissions('grafana')` (no folder/rule gating), so a user with Grafana create permission can get `[supported=true, allowed=true]`. Since `AlertRuleMenu` uses `(rulerSupported&&rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported&&grafanaAllowed)`, non-Grafana rules (Mimir/Loki etc., where skipToken is used) can incorrectly show actions like Duplicate based solely on Grafana permissions, even if the ruler ability is NotSupported. This is a real behavioral bug introduced by the skipToken path not returning NotSupported abilities.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AlertRuleMenu runs both useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities unconditionally for every rule, doubling ability computation and adding a useFolder subscription per rule in a hot component; prefer prom path only when rulerRule is absent
useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities/useRulerRuleAbilities memoize on actions, but AlertRuleMenu call sites pass inline array literals so the useMemo cache misses every render

adjudication.rationale: In `useAbilities.ts`, both `useRulerRuleAbilities` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` return `useMemo(() => actions.map(...), [abilities, actions])`. In `AlertRuleMenu.tsx`, both hooks are called with inline array literals (`[AlertRuleAction.Pause, ...]`). Because a new array instance is created on every render, the `actions` dependency changes every render, so the `useMemo` caches in these hooks will miss and recompute every render. This is a real, directly verifiable performance/ineffective-memoization issue introduced/used in the diff (even if the impact is likely minor).
